title: The 3-technique: how one defensive tackle wrecked Monday night (and how to spot him in your drill)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The original football-film-room repository wasn't reachable (access denied: "not configured for this session"). So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson builds on Lesson 24 (pass protection) and Lesson 32 (backup guards), using Monday night's game, where the brief's Bears pick was built on one defensive tackle.

The big idea: defensive linemen don't line up just anywhere.Coaches give each spot a number, called a technique. The number says which blocker he lines up on.The most dangerous spot for a pass-rushing tackle is the 3-technique.

Seen from above. White circles are the offensive line: left tackle (LT), left guard (LG), center (C), right guard (RG), right tackle (RT), tight end (TE). Yellow numbers are techniques. The numbers mirror on the left side. Yellow dot A is Jeffery Simmons on Monday night.

  1. A. The 3-technique lines up on the outside shoulder of a guard.That puts him in the B gap, the space between the guard and the tackle.Monday, Chicago's new DT Jeffery Simmons often lined up there, against Seattle's left side: Quenton Nelson at LG (in his first game for Seattle) and backup Josh Jones at LT (Charles Cross was out).
  2. B. The numbers. 0 is head-up on the center. 1 is on the center's shoulder. 2 is over a guard, 3 is outside the guard. 4 is over a tackle, 5 is outside the tackle. 7 is inside a tight end.Lower number = closer to the ball. Close to the ball, the center and a guard can both block you: a double-team.That's why big run-stuffers play the 0 or 1 ("nose tackle"). They eat double-teams so linebackers run free.
  3. C. Why the 3 is special. He usually faces just one blocker, the guard. And he has a straight line through the B gap to the quarterback.If the guard can't handle him alone, the offense must slide the center over or keep a back in to help. That's one fewer receiver (Lesson 24).
  4. What happened Monday. Simmons had 3 tackles, a pressure and a sack in his first 10 snaps. He finished with 6 tackles, 2 for a loss, 1 sack, a QB hit and a batted pass (NFL.com, PFT).Seattle ran for only 81 yards. Jadarian Price: 10 carries, 29 yards. Sam Darnold was sacked 3 times and hit 6 times. Seattle went 1 of 11 on 3rd down.Final: Bears 34, Seahawks 17. The brief's Bears +3.5 won.
  5. The other side of it: Thursday. Jacksonville just lost DT DaVon Hamilton for the season (torn quad). He's an inside run-stuffer.Without him, the middle of the Jaguars' line gets thinner, and Baltimore will likely try to run at it. That's the risk on the brief's Jaguars lean.

How to use it in your drill: before the snap, find the defensive tackle lined up just outside a guard. That's the 3-technique. If he's a star and the guard or tackle next to him is a backup, expect the offense to help: a back stays in to block, or the QB throws quick (Lesson 39). On 1st down, expect the run to go away from him. Log your call, then watch where the ball actually went.

Why it matters for your bets: a star interior pass rusher against a backup lineman is one of the most specific edges there is. It shortens drives, kills 3rd downs and lowers the opponent's QB yards. That was the core of the Bears pick, and it's the first thing the brief checks on every injury report (the checklist under "How picks are made").

Real examples to watch (Pacific time): Thursday, Jaguars at Ravens (5:15 p.m., Prime Video): watch the middle of Jacksonville's line without Hamilton. Sunday night, Buccaneers at Bears (5:20 p.m., NBC): Simmons again, this time against Tampa Bay's interior.

Video: search YouTube for "3 technique defensive tackle explained," "defensive line techniques 0 1 3 5," and "Jeffery Simmons Bears Seahawks highlights."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 2: The box)

quiz.q: Where does a 3-technique defensive tackle line up?
o: On the outside shoulder of a guard
quiz.w: The 3 is outside the guard's shoulder, in the B gap between guard and tackle. That's where Jeffery Simmons lined up against Seattle's left side.

quiz.q: Why do big run-stuffers line up at the 0 or 1 technique?
o: It's the shortest way to the QB
Close to the ball, they take double-teams so linebackers run free
quiz.w: Near the center, two blockers can reach them. A nose tackle eats that double-team on purpose.

quiz.q: A star 3-technique faces a backup guard. On 1st down, where do you expect the run to go?
quiz.w: Offenses run away from the defender they can't block. Then watch for a back staying in to help on passing downs.

quiz.q: Monday night, how did Seattle's run game do against Simmons and the Bears?
o: 81 yards; Jadarian Price had 10 carries for 29
quiz.w: Seattle ran for 81 yards and went 1 of 11 on 3rd down. Bears 34, Seahawks 17.
